2: If Jewish workers performed work for a non-Jew and he sent them a barrel of wine as payment, if they have not yet received it as payment, it is permitted for them to say to him, "Before you send us this barrel, it should be yours, and you should give us money for it." But if they have received it as payment, it is prohibited (Rabbi Yerucham and the Rosh).

If one hires non-Jewish workers and provides them with food, it is prohibited to give them wine of libation. If he says to them, "Go and drink from the store of so-and-so, and I will pay," it is permitted, even if he designated a coin for them and it is in the possession of the homeowner. However, if he designated a coin for them beforehand, it is prohibited, specifically when he said to him, "This coin should be in your hand until you give the workers to drink, and I will settle with you later." But if he gave it to him to take out now if he needs it, it is permitted.
